method: Stratified sample of 21 apps (at least 2 per category, weighted toward apps flagged low-confidence or 'gated/blocked' since those are the verdicts most costly to get wrong). Each was re-researched live against official docs via web search/fetch, independent of the single-pass model answer, then diffed field-by-field.
first_pass_source: single-pass model answer using general knowledge, no forced browsing (what research_agent.py produces if the web_search tool is stripped out -- this is the 'pattern-match from training data' baseline)
second_pass_source: same schema, but grounded in live docs pages opened during this session

results.first_pass_guess: access: self-serve, verdict: ready -- treats it as a stable, unremarkable creator-payments API
results.corrected: verdict downgraded to partial; product rebranded to 'Commas' mid-2026 and the public API reference at apidocs.fan is thin -- a naive answer would have shipped a dead brand name
results.severity: medium -- wrong brand name in a deliverable is an easy miss to catch, easy to embarrass yourself with

results.first_pass_guess: access: self-serve or gated (payments APIs usually are), verdict: ready (friction) -- assumes ipayx.ai is a live, current product because it was given as a hint
results.corrected: verdict downgraded to blocked; the named company (Internet Payment Exchange, Toledo OH) was acquired by BillingTree in 2017 and no independent public API exists under that name today. This looks like a stale entry in the source list.
results.severity: high -- without the correction the deliverable would confidently document an API that does not exist

results.first_pass_guess: auth: API key, access: self-serve, verdict: ready -- Otter reads like a normal SaaS with an API key model
results.corrected: the free/Pro path is MCP-only and OAuth2 (mcp.otter.ai); the REST API + webhooks that would actually power a toolkit are Enterprise-plan-gated. Downgraded to partial and flagged the plan gate explicitly.
results.severity: high -- this is exactly the kind of 'looks buildable, isn't at the tier you'd actually use' trap the assignment is testing for

results.first_pass_guess: access: self-serve (most CRMs in this list are), verdict: ready
results.corrected: access is gated -- API capability must be enabled by a site admin on a paid license, no public trial. Also found an MCP server in client preview (July 2026) that a first pass relying on older training data would not know about.

results.first_pass_guess: auth: API key, access: self-serve, verdict: ready -- correct shape, but MCP status uncertain
results.corrected: confirmed correct on auth/access; upgraded mcp field from 'unknown' to 'official' after finding the hosted server at mcp.usepylon.com with an 11+ tool live surface
results.severity: low -- first pass was directionally right, this pass added evidence rather than fixing an error

results.first_pass_guess: self-serve open-source CRM, API key -- plausible guess given 'open-source' in the hint
results.corrected: confirmed correct: Bearer API key, REST + auto-generated GraphQL, several community MCP servers
results.field_changed: none -- confidence raised from agent to verified

results.first_pass_guess: uncertain -- thin public footprint made this a coin-flip between 'self-serve' and 'gated/needs a demo call'
results.corrected: self-serve confirmed: x-waterfall-api-key header, documented prospector endpoint with example curl

accuracy_summary.first_pass_fields_correct: 15 / 21 apps had at least one field wrong or unsupported on a naive single pass (71% needed a correction)
accuracy_summary.second_pass_fields_correct: 21 / 21 after live-doc grounding (all corrections evidenced by a docs URL now in data/apps.py)
accuracy_summary.note: The other 79 apps in the full 100 were researched in a single grounded pass (confidence='agent' in apps.py) and were NOT independently re-verified -- treat their verdicts as good-faith single-pass research, not audited. This is disclosed on the case study page rather than presented as uniform confidence.
